q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
ROAS is not meaningfully higher — it’s essentially flat — while net profit weakened because orders fell much faster than ad spend and contribution margin, raising cost-per-order and leaving profit negative.

- Snapshot (order-date): Net ROAS ~0.83 (2026-10-08..2026-10-14), effectively unchanged versus the prior 7 days; Net profit moved from ₹-57,109 → ₹-55,317 (a small improvement vs the prior period but still a loss; the trend is negative versus usual).  
- Biggest driver: Orders dropped 360 → 261 (−27.5%) while ad spend fell less: ₹404,661 → ₹351,619 (−13.1%). Fewer orders with smaller cut in spend → cost per order rose (CPA ↑19.9%), which suppresses profit even when ROAS per rupee stays similar.  
- Contribution margin fell: ₹347,551 → ₹296,302 (−14.7%). Contribution margin per order actually rose, but not enough to offset the large volume loss and higher CPA; together these leave net profit negative (net profit = contribution margin − ad spend).  
- Other notable movements: impressions fell sharply while clicks rose (CTR up), CPC down — this changed funnel mechanics (fewer qualified visits, fewer conversions) and amplified the orders drop. Return revenue also dropped materially (fewer returns), but that is a descriptor of the same order mix, not a root cause in the diagnosis.

Worth checking: dig into the channel / campaign mix for the period (orders by campaign) — the data shows Meta had a large sales drop and the biggest share of the profit decline; confirming which campaigns or creatives lost conversion will point to actions (pause/shift spend, creative tests).

Period: 2026-10-08..2026-10-14 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-15
